'''Altice Dominicana''' ('''Altice Dominicana, [[List of legal entity types by country#Dominican Republic|S.A.]]'''), [[doing business as]] '''[[Altice]]''' (formerly '''Tricom'''), is the second largest landline service provider in the Dominican Republic. Since 2013, it is part of the French Netherlands-based [[Altice (company)|Altice]]. It owns and operates a major [[High-definition television|HDTV]] [[Cable television|Cable TV]] service (which also operated under its former names "Telecable Nacional" and "Tricom") along with landline and wireless voice services. Its [[Internet service provider|ISP]] branch offers residential bandwidth with speeds up to 300&nbsp;Mbit/s and is also a national [[mobile network operator]].

== Background ==
In 1988, Zona Franca de San Isidro spawned San Isidro Teleport, which was later renamed Tricom. In 1990, the company had reached an agreement with the Dominican Republic to provide communications services nationwide.

== Timeline ==
On May 20, 1992, the company began to implement "Long Distance Call Centers", entering the business of international long-distance services.

In 1993, Tricom sold [[Motorola]] a 40% stake in the company with a goal of improving their local and international infrastructure.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Ancochea |first1=Diego Sánchez |title=Domestic Capital, Civil Servants and the State: Costa Rica and the Dominican Republic under Globalisation |journal=Journal of Latin American Studies |date=November 2005 |volume=37 |issue=4 |pages=709–710 |doi=10.1017/S0022216X05009831 |s2cid=144906454 |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-latin-american-studies/article/abs/domestic-capital-civil-servants-and-the-state-costa-rica-and-the-dominican-republic-under-globalisation/BA51C9698572C471AFC4DA1FD84BADC2 |language=en |issn=1469-767X|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

On November 17, 1994, Tricom and [[Claro República Dominicana|CODETEL]] connected their telephone exchanges, allowing a massive installation of residential lines. Following is the implementation of pagers, paging services, and mobile products. In 1995 the first long-distance prepaid card, "Efectiva", was made public.

In 1996, Tricom implemented Motorola's Digital Telephone services which allowed the installation of residential and business lines in just 48 hours. Amigo, the country's first prepaid wireless provider, is launched in 1997. Meanwhile, TRICOM USA is created to offer long-distance services to the Hispanic community in [[New York City]].

In 1998, Tricom placed 5,700,000 shares of common [[Share capital|stock]] in the [[New York Stock Exchange|New York Stock Exchange (NYSE)]], becoming the first Dominican company to be listed in the U.S. stock market.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Newswires |first1=Dow Jones |title=Tricom's ADRs Begin Trading On New York Stock Exchange |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB894410803708355000#:~:text=May%206%2C%201998%2012%3A01%20am%20ET%20NEW%20YORK,Class%20A%20common%20shares%20priced%20at%20%2413%20each. |access-date=21 February 2022 |work=Wall Street Journal |date=6 May 1998|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

In 1999, the company achieved 300,000 customers, becoming the leader in mobile communications in addition to servicing 68% of the country's landlines.

In 2004, the company was de-listed from the [[New York Stock Exchange|NYSE]].

On June 5, 2012, Tricom announced their intent to begin a buildout of a [[Hybrid fibre-coaxial]] network across [[Bayahibe]], [[Bonao]], [[Casa de Campo, Dominican Republic|Casa de Campo]], [[La Romana Province|La Romana]], [[La Vega Province|La Vega]], [[San Cristóbal Province|San Cristóbal]], [[San Francisco de Macorís]], [[San Pedro de Macorís]], [[Santiago de los Caballeros|Santiago]], and [[Santo Domingo]].<ref>{{Citation |url=http://www.tricom.net/SiteArticlesview.aspx?ArticleID=108 |title=Tricom con nueva red de Fibra Óptica |work=Tricom |language=es |access-date=April 18, 2013 |date=June 5, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130412213204/http://www.tricom.net/SiteArticlesview.aspx?ArticleID=108 |archive-date=2013-04-12 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On July 4, 2012, Tricom announced they were going to begin a build out of a [[LTE (telecommunication)|4G-LTE]] network.<ref>{{Citation |url=http://www.tricom.net/SiteArticlesview.aspx?ArticleID=111 |title=Tricom inicia proceso de implementación de una nueva red móvil 4G-LTE |work=Tricom |language=es |access-date=April 18, 2013 |date=July 4, 2012}}</ref>

On March 13, 2013, Tricom launched a [[video on demand]] service, becoming the second Dominican provider after [[Claro República Dominicana]] to offer a VOD service.<ref>{{Citation |url=http://www.tricom.net/SiteArticlesview.aspx?ArticleID=122 |title=Telecable Tricom introduce nuevo servicio de Video On Demand |work=Tricom |language=es |access-date=April 18, 2013 |date=March 13, 2013}}</ref>

On March 18, 2013, Tricom launched their [[LTE (telecommunication)|4G-LTE]] network and became the second Dominican provider after [[Orange S.A.|Orange]] to offer LTE for modems.<ref>{{Citation |url=http://www.tricom.net/SiteArticlesview.aspx?ArticleID=124 |title=Tricom Introduce La Evolucion Del Internet Movil 4G LTE |work=Tricom |language=es |access-date=April 18, 2013 |date=March 18, 2013}}</ref>

On May 2, 2013, Tricom launched their LTE network for mobile phones, becoming the first Dominican provider to offer LTE for mobiles.<ref>{{Citation |url=http://www.tricom.net/pageview.aspx?ArticleID=126 |title=Tricom Con El Primer Smartphone 4G LTE Del País |work=Tricom |language=es |access-date=May 1, 2013 |date=May 2, 2013}}</ref>

On November 27, 2013, Orange sold its Dominican unit to Tricom's Parent company, Altice, for US$1.435 billion.<ref>{{cite news |title=Orange agrees Dominican Republic unit sale to Altice |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/orange-altice-idUSWEB00EVY20131127 |access-date=21 February 2022 |work=Reuters |date=27 November 2013 |language=en}}</ref> The merger was approved and finalized on November 21, 2017, with the Orange and Tricom brand names permanently retired and both of Tricom's and Orange's Cellular networks integrated to Altice's own cellular network. The company began using the Altice name as their brand for their services.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.elcaribe.com.do/2017/11/21/presentan-oficialmente-a-altice-dominicana|title = Presentan oficialmente a Altice Dominicana|date = 21 November 2017}}</ref>
